R0098.title: Fake Identity Authentication
R0098.definition: A fake identity refers to a person or entity using fictitious or forged identity information to conceal their true identity or purpose.
R0098.description: This may include using false names, addresses, dates of birth, social security numbers, and other personal information. Fake identities are typically used to deceive, evade legal liability, commit fraud, carry out cyberattacks, or engage in other improper activities.
R0098.influence: Affects the platform's compliance, security, credibility, user experience, and business operations.

observables: The same face or ID card is reused across multiple accounts during real-name authentication
Liveness detection shows anomalous features such as photo replay, masks, or deepfakes
The same device completes authentication for many different identities within a short window
The authenticated identity information is inconsistent with the home region of the bound phone number or bank card
Post-authentication account behavior does not match the declared identity scenario (e.g., a student account conducting large transactions)
